instructions.original_snippets: NEVER start a bash script without set -euo pipefail
instructions.content: Never start a bash script without set -euo pipefail; without all three flags, errors, unset variables, and pipeline failures are silently ignored.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use unquoted variable expansions in command arguments
instructions.content: Never leave a variable expansion unquoted in a command argument; word splitting and glob expansion cause subtle bugs on values with spaces or special characters.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use ls | grep to filter files
instructions.content: Never pipe ls into grep to filter files; ls output is not reliably parseable and breaks on filenames with special characters.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER hardcode absolute paths for tools like python, node, or bash
instructions.content: Never hardcode an absolute interpreter path; paths differ across operating systems and distributions.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use eval to execute dynamically constructed commands
instructions.content: Never use eval on dynamically constructed commands; it enables code injection when any part comes from user input or external data.

instructions.original_snippets: Register a trap on EXIT (and ideally ERR, INT, TERM) that calls a cleanup function
instructions.content: Register a trap on EXIT (and ideally ERR, INT, TERM) before doing anything destructive, so a failed run cleans up after itself.

instructions.original_snippets: Verify that required external commands exist using command -v or equivalent
instructions.content: Verify every required external command exists with command -v before using it.

instructions.original_snippets: Use readonly for at least one script-level constant
instructions.content: Use readonly for script-level constants that must not change after initialization.

instructions.original_snippets: Write status/progress messages to stderr, not stdout
instructions.content: Write status and log messages to stderr so they never get piped into a script's actual output.

instructions.original_snippets: Include timestamps in log/status messages using date
No hardcoded passwords, connection strings, or tokens -- rely on environment variables
instructions.content: Never hardcode credentials in a script; read them from the environment instead.

instructions.original_snippets: Validate inputs with a regex allowlist and die on mismatch
instructions.content: Validate user-supplied input against an explicit allowlist pattern and die on mismatch, rather than trusting it.

instructions.original_snippets: Avoid useless cat: grep pattern file not cat file | grep pattern
instructions.content: Avoid a useless use of cat piped into another command that can read the file itself.
Keep each function focused on one responsibility.

instructions.original_snippets: Avoid bash arrays, [[ ]], $BASH_SOURCE for POSIX sh portability; test with sh -n script.sh
instructions.content: For POSIX sh portability, avoid bash-only constructs (arrays, [[ ]], $BASH_SOURCE) and verify with sh -n.

instructions.original_snippets: die() function that prints to stderr and exits non-zero
instructions.content: Define a die() helper that logs to stderr and exits non-zero, and call it from every failure path.
